title: Automotive Maintenance Technician (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC I&L
raw_text:
2.     MOS 3521, Automotive Maintenance Technician (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC I&L

    a. Summary. The Automotive Maintenance Technician services, inspects,
maintains, and repairs motor transport equipment at the field level.

       b.    Prerequisites

             (1) Must possess an EL score of 100 or MM score of 100 or higher.

             (2) Must possess normal vision to include acuity, color, and field of
vision.

    c. Requirements. Must complete the Automotive Maintenance Technician
Basic Course (M0335H7), Marine Corps Combat Service Support School, Camp
Lejeune, NC.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (x), Motor Transport Training and Readiness Manual.

       e.    Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

             (1) Automotive Service Technicians and Mechanics 49-3023.

        (2) Electrical and Electronic Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and
Repairers 49-2096.

       f.    Related Military Skill

             (1) Engineer Equipment Mechanic, 1341.

             (2) Light Armored Vehicle (LAV) Repairer/Technician, 2147.
common_text: The Motor Transport Occupational Field (OccFld) includes the licensing, operation, employment, maneuver, and maintenance functions for motor transport tactical wheeled vehicles and equipment in support of combat and garrison operations. Qualifications required include operation and maintenance skills of automotive vehicles. The duties require highly technical skills supplemented by administrative and managerial skills. Motor Transport Marines will be required to learn licensing procedures, vehicle operation and maintenance procedures, personnel and operational management techniques, preparation of orders and directives and record keeping procedures. Formal schooling and standardized training is provided to Marines entering this Occupational Field. Types of entry-level jobs available include work as Tactical Wheeled Vehicle Operator and Field/ Intermediate Maintenance Technician. There is a wide variety of billets available in the OccFld ranging from duty at all staff levels of MAGTF to the opportunity to serve in smaller organizations/units.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
